L275@P3: on rs6897932, which we genotyped in two independent northern

L277@P3: The PDT analysis confirmed a significant association with multiple

L584@P6: METHODS
L585@P6: US family data set. The data set consisted of 760 stringently ascertained
L586@P6: families with multiple sclerosis (563 single-case and 197 multiple-case families),
L587@P6: which included 1,055 sampled affected individuals with multiple sclerosis. All
L588@P6: known ancestors were non-Hispanic individuals of European descent. Diagnostic criteria and ascertainment protocols have been summarized elsewhere38,39. All affected family members were examined or had their medical
L589@P6: records reviewed by one of the authors (S.L.H.); 83% could be classified by
L590@P6: disease subtype as having relapsing-remitting (RR), secondary progressive (SP),
L591@P6: progressive-relapsing (PR) or primary progressive (PP) multiple sclerosis.
L592@P6: SPMS was defined by six months of worsening neurological disability not
L593@P6: explained by relapse and measured as a deterioration of either (i) one or more
L594@P6: points on the expanded disability status scale (EDSS) in affected individuals
L595@P6: with an EDSS o6 or (ii) a one-half point or more for those with an EDSS 46.
L596@P6: PPMS was defined by the presence of both (i) progressive clinical worsening
L597@P6: for more than 12 months from symptom onset without any relapses and
L598@P6: (ii) abnormal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), as defined by the presence of two or
L599@P6: more oligoclonal bands or an elevated IgG index in the CSF. If acute relapses
L600@P6: were superimposed on this steadily progressive course, individuals were
L601@P6: considered to have PRMS.
L602@P6: The family collection has been ongoing for 420 years, and disease
L603@P6: subtype information is not available on some of the first individuals with
L604@P6: multiple sclerosis collected (17%). The protocol was approved by the
L605@P6: Committee on Human Research at the University of California, San Francisco,
L606@P6: and informed consent was obtained from all participants. A clinical and
L607@P6: demographic description of the individuals with multiple sclerosis is shown
L608@P6: in Table 1.
L609@P6: US case-control data set. The case-control data set was ascertained through a
L610@P6: prospective study of phenotype-genotype-biomarker associations in a large
L611@P6: cohort of individuals with multiple sclerosis followed longitudinally (Table 1).
L612@P6: Individuals with multiple sclerosis (ages 18–65 years) who were evaluated in the
L613@P6: Multiple Sclerosis Center at the University of California, San Francisco between
L614@P6: July 2004 and September 2005 were invited to participate. This study preferentially recruited individuals with a recent onset of multiple sclerosis, although
L615@P6: individuals with all clinical subtypes (RRMS, SPMS, PRMS and PPMS)
L616@P6: participated. Therefore, there are more individuals with RRMS in the
L617@P6: case-control data set, whereas many individuals with RRMS in the familybased data set have progressed to SPMS since the time at which they were
L618@P6: first collected. Affected individuals were asked to invite a healthy control of the
L619@P6: same sex and ancestry and similar age range to participate in the study.
L620@P6: The protocol was approved by the Committee on Human Research at the
L621@P6: University of California, San Francisco, and informed consent was obtained
L622@P6: from all participants.
L623@P6: European family and case-control data sets. In the UK, trios (an affected
L624@P6: individual and both parents) and unrelated affected individuals were recruited
L625@P6: from across the country as part of an ongoing study of genetic susceptibility to
L626@P6: multiple sclerosis. In Belgium, trios and unrelated cases were recruited from
L627@P6: the region of Flanders. Diagnostic criteria were identical to those used in the
L628@P6: US, except that progressive-relapsing multiple sclerosis was not distinguished
L629@P6: from secondary progressive multiple sclerosis. In Belgium, relapsing-remitting
L630@P6: and secondary progressive multiple sclerosis were grouped together as ‘boutonset’. All individuals gave written informed consent, and the study was
L631@P6: approved by the Thames Valley Multicentre Research Ethics Committee
L632@P6: (UK) and the ethics committee of the University Hospital Gasthuisberg in
L633@P6: Leuven (Belgium), respectively. Unrelated UK control samples were obtained
L634@P6: from two sources: the Human Random Control (HRC) DNA panel (derived
L635@P6: from blood donors) supplied by the European Collection of Cell Cultures
L636@P6: (479 individuals) and the British 1958 Birth Cohort (2,047 individuals). Belgian
L637@P6: controls (n ¼ 199) were hospital staff and individuals with noninflammatory
L638@P6: neurological conditions.
L649@P6: Genomic DNA was extracted from whole blood using standard procedures.
L650@P6: We genotyped five common SNPs within MMP19, four SNPs within CCL2 and
L651@P6: fourteen SNPs within IL7R, including all significant SNPs in IL7R from a
L652@P6: previous study26. All SNP genotypes were generated by the TaqMan allelic
L653@P6: discrimination assay on an ABI7900HT genotyping platform, using the Assayon-Demand or Assay-by-Design service from Applied Biosystems. Duplicate
L654@P6: quality control samples were placed both within and across plates, and
L655@P6: matching genotypes were required for the genotype data to be included in
L656@P6: the analysis. Laboratory personnel were unaware of pedigree structure, affection
L657@P6: status and location of quality control samples. All SNPs were required to have
L658@P6: at least 95% genotyping efficiency, and SNP rs6897932 had 97% efficiency.

L682@P6: For the family-based data sets, we used the PDT6 for single-locus association
L683@P6: testing, and the HBAT module of the FBAT package48 for haplotype analysis
L684@P6: (using the ‘hbat –e’ command line option). The SNP-specific maximum
L685@P6: number of informative discordant sibling pairs in the US data set was 807
L686@P6: (395 from multiplex and 412 from singleton families), and the maximum
L687@P6: number of informative parent-offspring trios in the US data set was 479 (151
L688@P6: from multiplex and 328 from singleton families). Multiple sclerosis severity
L689@P6: scores (MSSS) were calculated as described previously10. Age of onset and
L690@P6: MSSS were analyzed with the QTDT package8, using the Monks-Kaplan test7.
L691@P6: The case-control data sets were analyzed by logistic regression (SAS), using an
L692@P6: additive allele coding of genotypes (0 for homozygous carriers of the major
L693@P6: allele, 1 for heterozygous genotypes, 2 for homozygous carriers of the minor
L694@P6: allele) as a screening test for all SNPs. The genotype frequencies in multiple
L695@P6: sclerosis cases and controls suggested a recessive model for SNP rs6897932 at
L696@P6: IL7Ra, which was used for the joint analysis of the US and European data sets
L697@P6: (Table 4), for the combined analysis of HLA and IL7R (Table 5) and for the

L699@P6: NATURE GENETICS ADVANCE ONLINE PUBLICATION 7
L700@P6-7: ARTICLESpower calculations performed with QUANTO49. The P values from the logistic
L701@P7: regression model were very similar with and without adjustment for age
L702@P7: (continuous) and gender (categorical). Permutation-based association testing
L703@P7: and haplotype analysis were performed with the WHAP program13. The
L704@P7: method implemented in WHAP uses a weighted maximum-likelihood
L705@P7: approach to allow for ambiguity in statistically inferred haplotypes.

locators.section: Results: differential splicing and allele-specific expression; Figure 2
locators.excerpt:
L354@P4: The effect of rs6897932 on differential splicing of IL7R
L355@P4: The alternative splicing of IL7R has potent consequences for the
L356@P4: function of the receptor, as transcripts that include exon 6 encode a
L357@P4: membrane-bound IL7Ra, whereas transcripts that skip exon 6 encode
L358@P4: a soluble form of the protein14. To test whether the alternate ‘C’
L359@P4: and ‘T’ alleles of rs6897932 could affect the inclusion of exon 6,
L360@P4: we cloned the two allelic versions of exon 6 and the surrounding
L361@P4: intronic sequences into the alternative splicing minigene construct
L362@P4: pI-11 (ref. 15). Analysis of transcripts from the two minigenes showed
L363@P4: that the multiple sclerosis–associated ‘C’ allele resulted in an approximately twofold increase in the skipping of exon 6 compared with
L364@P4: transcripts containing the ‘T’ allele (Fig. 2). The data are consistent
L365@P4: with at least two possible mechanisms: the multiple sclerosis–
L366@P4: associated ‘C’ allele weakens an exonic splicing enhancer (ESE),
L367@P4: or it augments an exonic splicing silencer (ESS). The latter is more
L368@P4: likely, as transversions at rs6897932 to either a G or an A nucleotide
L369@P4: substantially decreased exon skipping (for example, production of
L370@P4: soluble IL7Ra), and substitutions adjacent to the SNP essentially
L371@P4: abolished skipping (Fig. 2). Thus, our results are consistent with
L372@P4: the presence of a weak ESS that mediates a low level of exon 6
L373@P4: skipping, resulting in about 10% soluble IL7Ra. Our data suggest a
L374@P4: functional role for the alternative rs6897932 alleles on the splicing of
L375@P4: exon 6 in IL7R.
L376@P4: Allele-specific expression of IL7R
L377@P4: We analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 94 healthy
L378@P4: controls by quantitative real-time PCR to detect differential expression
L379@P4: of IL7R using one amplicon that spanned exons 6–7 and two control
L380@P4: amplicons spanning exons 4–5 and exons 7–8, respectively. Using
L381@P4: analysis of variance with Bonferroni correction, we observed significantly lower expression of the exon 6–7 amplicon for carriers of the
L382@P4: multiple sclerosis–associated ‘C’ allele (P ¼ 0.015); the two control
L383@P4: amplicons (exons 4–5 and 7–8) did not show significantly different
L384@P4: expression by genotype. Consistent with our in vitro experiments, this
L385@P4: suggests that carriers of the ‘C’ allele at rs6897932 produce less
L386@P4: membrane-bound IL7Ra protein compared with carriers of the
L387@P4: ‘T’ allele, leading to a further increase of the soluble form of IL7Ra.
L388@P4: This hypothesis is supported by our previous report that interleukin-7
L389@P4: (IL7) function and IL7Ra expression in T cells is reduced in individuals with multiple sclerosis16.

locators.section: Methods: cell culture and allele-specific PCR
locators.excerpt:
L711@P7: Analysis of exon 6 inclusion in cell culture. To amplify exon 6 of IL7R via
L712@P7: PCR, we used genomic DNA from two phenotypically normal individuals who
L713@P7: were homozygous for the ‘C’ or ‘T’ alleles of rs6897932. The last 614
L714@P7: nucleotides of intron 5, the entire exon 6 and the first 573 nucleotides of
L715@P7: intron 6 of IL7R were amplified and cloned between the XbaI and XhoI sites in
L716@P7: the splicing reporter minigene pI-11 (ref. 15), to create splicing reporters pI-11-
L717@P7: IL7R172 and pI-11-IL7R382.
L718@P7: We created mutants of the minigenes with either A or G at rs6897932 and
L719@P7: also created a version of pI-11-IL7R382 in which 3 nt upstream and 3 nt
L720@P7: downstream of this locus were mutated (TAA[T]CAT - GCC[T]ACG). All
L721@P7: constructs and subclones were sequenced. The sequences of these constructs
L722@P7: and subclones and the oligonucleotides used in their construction are available
L723@P7: upon request.
L724@P7: Rat DT3 and AT3 cells were cultured in low-glucose DMEM (Gibco) with
L725@P7: 10% FBS. HeLa cells were cultured in high-glucose DMEM with 10% FBS.
L726@P7: Stable transfections (Fig. 2b) were as described in ref. 50. Transient transfections (Fig. 2c) used the same stable transfection protocol, except that 100 ng of
L727@P7: DNA was transfected in cells, and cells were harvested 48 h post-transfection
L728@P7: without any selection. All transfections were performed in triplicate for
L729@P7: each construct.
L730@P7: Total RNA was extracted from stable cells using Trizol reagent (Invitrogen)
L731@P7: according to the manufacturer’s protocol, and exon 6 inclusion was determined
L732@P7: by RT-PCR analysis as previously described15,50. PCR products were loaded
L733@P7: directly on a 5% polyacrylamide nondenaturing gel, electrophoresed at 100 V
L734@P7: for 3–4 h and exposed to Amersham Hyperfilm-MP or Molecular Dynamics
L735@P7: phosphorimager screens. Quantification of PCR products was performed with
L736@P7: ImageQuant software (Molecular Dynamics). In each case, RT-PCR products
L737@P7: were normalized for molar equivalence.
L738@P7: Stable minigene transfection. Rat DT3 cells were cultured in low-glucose
L739@P7: DMEM (Gibco) with 10% FBS. Stable transfections were as described in
L740@P7: ref. 50. All transfections were performed in triplicate for each construct, as
L741@P7: described above.
L742@P7: Allele-specific IL7R isoform expression in healthy controls. Real-time PCR
L743@P7: was carried out in 94 control individuals using Applied Biosystems TaqMan
L744@P7: one-step real-time PCR master mix reagents kit under the manufacturer’s
L745@P7: recommended conditions on an ABI 7900HT Sequence Detection System using
L746@P7: SDS 2.0 software. Positive and negative controls, as well as a calibration curve
L747@P7: spanning five orders of magnitude constructed with an in vitro–transcribed
L748@P7: clone of GAPDH, all in triplicate, were also included in each reaction plate.
L749@P7: Amplification values are expressed as 1012/2ct. Three different gene expression
L750@P7: TaqMan assays were tested: Hs00233682_m1, which covers the IL7R exon 4/5
L751@P7: boundary, Hs00904814_m1, which covers the exon 6/7 boundary, and
L752@P7: Hs00902338_g1, which covers the exon 7/8 boundary.
